decisions.issues: Minor only: the tiny background riders at the gate wear ochre-orange turbans, not white or cream, but with white tunics and no red sash they cannot be mistaken for Nagoji. Otherwise clean: a Deccan hill fort on black rock, a thick bastion with cannon ports, lime-washed walls, hard sun, saffron swallow-tailed pennants, no figure close enough to identify, no text. There is plenty of open sky at the top left for both captions.

FAIL ear: Nagoji wears a stud with a gold teardrop hanging below the lobe. Minor: Ramayyan walks alongside Nagoji instead of already waiting on the path, and he wears toe-post sandals where his sheet shows him barefoot. Passes: clean-shaven chin, sleeves down to the wrists, boots, talwar, settling the sash, laterite quarters with a dripping tiled roof and palms, no text.
decisions.correction: Nagoji's ear ornament is a single tiny gold stud, about the size of a peppercorn, sitting flush on the front of the earlobe with NOTHING hanging from it: no drop, no bead, no pendant, no ring below the lobe. Keep everything else that worked: the laterite quarters with the tiled roof still dripping, wet path, coconut palms, Nagoji stepping out of the doorway settling his broad red sash, cream tunic sleeves down to the wrists, boots and talwar, thick curled moustache and clean-shaven chin. Ramayyan stands still on the path a few paces from the door, already waiting and facing it, barefoot with no sandals, palm-leaf bundle under one arm. Keep the upper right sky open and low-detail for two captions.

decisions.issues: Minor: Ramayyan holds a second stylus with his palm-leaf bundle as well as the one in his right hand. The house front (wooden veranda pillars, plastered wall) differs from 1.2's laterite doorway, but 1.2 needs regeneration anyway. Passes: a flush gold ball stud on the lobe with nothing hanging, clean-shaven chin, sleeves down to the wrists, boots, talwar at the left hip, Ramayyan turned to go with Nagoji a step behind, sound hands, no text. Open sky at the top centre and top right gives room for the speech balloon and the caption.

v01 fails: Nagoji wears a hanging gold drop earring, and village women wear stitched blouses, which is anachronistic against the bible's old Kerala drape. v02 passes the hard checks. Nagoji's ear has a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging, and his chin is clean-shaven. He wears the commander dress with sleeves to the wrists and is barefoot, as is Ramayyan. The boots stand side by side at the foot of the steps with the talwar laid across them. The gateway is a modest Kerala one: a two-tiered tiled roof on wooden posts over a laterite and stone base, with no tower. The temple sits on a hill above tiled houses and palms. Villagers in period cloth with no stitched blouses stand aside with joined palms, and Ramayyan gives them a small smiling nod. There is no text. Minor, not a fail: Nagoji climbs a couple of steps ahead of Ramayyan, though 1.3 has him following; the 1.4 script does not fix the order. Large open sky at upper left holds both captions.

v01 fails on a hanging gold drop earring. v02 passes: the region edit leaves one tiny flush gold stud on the lobe with nothing hanging. Moustache and chin are correct. Both men are barefoot; Nagoji carries no talwar, wears the commander dress and has his sleeves to the wrists. Ramayyan has turned back to face Nagoji, with receding hair, plain white cloth and no forehead marks. The courtyard has lamps, bells on chains, incense, Brahmins at ritual in the background, and the priest (thread, gold-bordered mundu, hair knot) holding a lamp tray in the sanctum doorway. Minor notes, not fails: the left door jamb of the sanctum carries a small dark carved band whose lower part has glyph-like marks; at panel size it reads as ornament, not lettering. The lobe edge where the drop was removed is slightly soft. Lettering space: Nagoji's balloon fits over the sky and hills at top left, and Ramayyan's over the dark roof beam and door lintel at top centre.

v02 passes every hard check. Nagoji has a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging, a clean-shaven chin, the rust-red turban, a cream tunic with sleeves to the wrist, the red sash and no talwar. His hands are sound and loosely clasped in front of the sash. Ramayyan matches his sheet, carries the palm-leaf bundle and stylus, and has the faint smile. The pillar lamps are now open brass bowls on brackets with bare flames, the standing lamp is brass with open wicks, and there is no glass anywhere. The frame cuts both men at the shin, so their feet do not show; no boots are visible, so the barefoot rule is not contradicted. There is no text and no chair. The bright courtyard is behind them at left and the lit sanctum ahead at right. Lettering space: the sky at top left and the dark stone wall at top right. v01 is rejected: enclosed glass box-lanterns on the pillars break the Kerala open-lamp rule, and Nagoji's hands are joined in prayer, which the script does not ask for.

Passes all hard checks. Nagoji has a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging and a clean-shaven chin, with the hand at his jaw kept below the lip line. His sleeves reach the wrists, he carries no talwar, and there is no text. The three insets (kalari boys with sticks, women sorting pepper on mats, a bullock cart of paddy sacks) sit along the top inside the frame. A clear sky band between the insets and his head takes both balloons. Minor, non-blocking: (1) the pepper-sorting women wear stitched short-sleeved blouses, which are doubtful for 1740s Kerala; earlier chapters treated this as non-blocking. (2) His head is in three-quarter view, close to but not a strict profile. (3) He stands at the bright edge of the courtyard rather than in the mandapa shade, but the temple matches 2.1. Feet are out of frame. Ramayyan speaks from off panel to the right, where he stood in 2.1.

v02 is acceptable. Ramayyan is in right profile facing the lamp-lit, garlanded sanctum, with receding hair, plain unbordered white cloth and no forehead marks. He has exactly two hands, and his right index finger counts against the raised left hand. One digit of the left hand reads as folded down, which fits counting. He holds no stylus, and the palm-leaf bundle is clamped under his near (right) upper arm with no extra hand under it. An old dark water stain is on the stone ceiling, just above and ahead of him. The hanging lamp is open brass on a chain, and the niche lamps are open. There is no text, chair or anachronism. Minor point (not a failure): his near shoulder and arm are bare under the drape, while 2.1, 2.4 and 1.5 show a short-sleeved under-tunic. Lettering space: the sky at top left and the plain ceiling to the right of the stain. Nagoji is off panel to the left, behind Ramayyan. v01 is rejected: a third hand is drawn under the palm-leaf bundle while both hands also count, and he holds a stylus.

Passes the hard checks. Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin sharp features, receding hair with curly black hair behind, plain unbordered white cloth, no forehead marks or sacred thread. Both hands are sound, one holding the stylus and one holding the palm-leaf bundle. No text is written on the leaves, every lamp has an open brass wick, and the setting matches the temple on this page. Minor: this is a chest-up medium close-up rather than a tight close-up. He looks down at the leaves as he writes, and the lamplight shows only as catchlights in his eyes and the brass lamp beside him. The writing fits his ledger line. The sky between his head and the temple roof, the roof tiles at top right and the plain wall to the right of his face give room for three balloons without covering his face or hands.

Passes the hard checks. Nagoji has a tiny flush gold stud, a clean-shaven chin, sleeves down and no talwar. Ramayyan matches his sheet and holds the palm-leaf bundle. The wall of lit niches has open-wick lamps throughout. A landed woman lights a niche with her two attendants, and an older man stands in a white mundu. Through the open gateway, a fisherman with a net and a labourer stay outside and hand a brass oil pot to a temple servant on the threshold. There is no text and no glass. Minor, non-blocking: (1) the landed woman and her attendants wear stitched short-sleeved blouses, which are doubtful for 1740s Kerala; earlier chapters let the same thing pass. (2) Nagoji and Ramayyan are larger than 'small' at the left edge, though in shadow, and their feet are cropped so barefoot is not visible. (3) The script marks both lines as off-panel, but Ramayyan is drawn in frame, so the tails point to his mouth. The sky and wooded hill above the niche wall give a clear upper band for the two long balloons.

FAILS ear check: Nagoji's ear ornament is a gold bell-shaped drop hanging below the lobe, not a flush stud. FAILS sleeves check: both tunic sleeves are rolled up above the elbows, leaving the forearms bare (bible 10 @3-8.5: sleeves down to the wrists). The rest is good: wide awninged market, Arab merchant cross-legged on the platform with brass scale and silver coins, servant at the pepper sacks, clean-shaven Syrian Christian scribe with a wooden cross writing at the desk, Ramayyan with his palm-leaf bundle, Nagoji in boots with talwar, laterite fort, no text. Neighbour conflict: the woman with the baby at the cloth stall wears a red sari with gold and jasmine, but in 3.4 the stallholder wears plain undyed cotton with no gold and no jasmine.
decisions.correction: Nagoji's ear ornament must be a tiny round gold stud sitting flush on the front of the earlobe with nothing hanging below it: no bell, no bead, no drop. Both sleeves of his cream tunic are worn DOWN to the wrists, not rolled or pushed up, so no bare forearm shows on either arm. Keep everything else exactly as it is: the wide awninged market with palm-leaf and cloth shades, the Arab merchant in white sitting cross-legged on the raised platform weighing silver coins on the small brass scale, his servant at the pepper sacks, the clean-shaven young Syrian Christian scribe in white cloth with a small wooden cross writing at the low desk beside the cloth stall, Marakkar men bargaining over pepper, Ramayyan with his palm-leaf bundle and stylus, Nagoji entering in boots with the talwar at his sash, and the red laterite fort beyond. The woman with the baby at the cloth stall is the stallholder of the next panels: plain undyed cotton mundu with a cloth over the shoulder, no stitched blouse, no gold, no jasmine, hair in a simple knot.

decisions.issues: v01 fails the ear check: a gold drop hangs below Nagoji's lobe. v02 (ear region edit) passes every hard check: a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves down to the wrists, red sash, boots and talwar. Ramayyan matches his sheet (receding curly hair, white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus) and looks off down the row of stalls while Nagoji looks unimpressed, so the beat reads. No text, no anachronism. Open sky top right and awning top left give room for all three balloons. Soft continuity notes, not failures: the background stallholder at the left wears a maroon stitched blouse with a gold necklace and earrings, and the background scribe wears a sleeveless white vest with no cross. In 3.3 v02 she is in plain undyed cotton with no gold, as script 3.4 asks, and the scribe is in white cloth with a cross. Ramayyan wears sandals (barefoot on his sheet), which is fine for the market.

v01 fails. Yusuf wears a long navy coat (not a short one) and carries a sword, the scribe has a beard although the script makes him clean-shaven, and the stallholder wears a stitched blouse and gold, which contradicts the plain no-gold look of 3.4. v02 is acceptable. Yusuf is tall and lean with a white skullcap, a neatly trimmed dark beard, no scar, no turban, and a short brown coat over a white tunic, leaning across the cloth table toward the stallholder, so he does not read as Ibrahim. Pepper sacks are stacked behind the stall. The clean-shaven young scribe in white cloth with a wooden cross writes on paper at the back of the table. The stallholder wears plain undyed cotton with no gold, her hair in a simple knot, and holds the baby on her hip, which matches 3.4. Both of Yusuf's hands are braced on the cloth, the far hand above the near one. They are slightly crowded but anatomically sound. No text, no anachronism. A large open sky at the upper right holds the caption and Yusuf's balloon. One soft note: the stallholder's costume differs from her background appearance in 3.2 v02 (maroon blouse and gold there).

Passes the hard checks. The stallholder is in her late twenties, with the baby on her hip, arms folded, plain undyed cotton mundu with a shoulder cloth, hair in a simple knot, no jasmine, an immovable look. The stall matches 3.3 (cloth stacks, pepper sacks, hanging brass lamp). No text, sound anatomy, and the hanging grey cloth behind her plus the open sky at right leave room for the caption and balloons. Minor: she wears a tiny gold ear drop (the script says no gold). The figure writing at the next table is a bare-shouldered young man with a topknot rather than the Syrian Christian scribe. Framing is medium-wide rather than close. Note: 3.3 v01 and 3.5 v01 dress her in a maroon blouse with gold, which conflicts with this script-correct panel.

Passes the hard checks. Nagoji has a flush gold ear stud with nothing hanging, a clean-shaven chin (light texture only), a thick moustache, sleeves to the wrists and the talwar at his sash. Ramayyan and Nagoji in the foreground watch Yusuf. Yusuf is mid-laugh with his eyes cut sideways toward the pale Dutch factor, who sits small in the mid-background in a 1740s dark long-skirted coat, knee breeches, stockings, buckled shoes and a black tricorne (not a blue-coated soldier). The inset of the scribe's pen sits inside the frame, and its mark is too small to read. No text. Minor: the background woman with the baby (the stallholder) wears a maroon stitched blouse with a gold necklace and earrings, which conflicts with 3.4's plain undyed cotton. The inset shows a cord-bound wooden tablet rather than paper. Yusuf's coat is dark brown here but navy in 3.3 v01 (3.3 is being regenerated to match). Lettering space is a narrow top band of awning cloth and sky: keep Ramayyan's two balloons in it and off the background woman's face.

v02 passes every hard check. The region edit fixed the ear: Nagoji now wears a small gold stud sitting on the front of the lobe with nothing hanging below it. It is a slightly elongated oval rather than a round dot, but there is no loop or drop, and the edit leaves no seam. Clean-shaven chin with thick curled moustache, rust-red turban, sleeves down to the wrists, red sash, talwar, boots. Ramayyan matches his sheet (thin, receding curly hair, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus). The red laterite fort has sloping tiled gatehouse roofs and no flag. No text, sound hands, and open sky upper right plus the plain canvas awning upper centre for the two balloons. v01 FAILS the ear check (a gold ball hangs from a loop below the lobe). Minor, not blocking: the background woman with the baby at the cloth stall wears a green stitched blouse, a red sari, a gold necklace, bangles and earrings. That conflicts with the plain undyed cotton stallholder of 3.4, and a stitched blouse is doubtful for 1740s Kerala. Ramayyan wears sandals (his sheet and 4.3 v02 show him barefoot). The pair still walk alongside the last stalls toward camera, with the fort off to the right, not out on the track with the fort ahead.

Hard checks pass: Nagoji's ear is a small flush gold stud with nothing hanging; chin clean-shaven with thick curled moustache; sleeves down; talwar; feet out of frame, so boots cannot be checked. Ramayyan matches his sheet. The drill master matches the script: stained, faded brown long-skirted coat with deep cuffs, bare-headed, grizzled hair tied back, stubble, soft belly, scowl, turned toward the pair. Men in white with white turbans stand in lines; no text; hands are sound. Minor: a plain cream flag flies on the fort tower at top right (the script asks for no European flag; a plain white flag could read as French colours or a truce flag). It sits in the sky where the drill master's balloon will likely cover it. The drill master is not noticeably short. The long guns show no clear matchlock detail.

FAIL script beat: the drill master is absent. Nagoji stands at the near flank of the firing line with his arm flung out and his mouth open shouting the command, so he takes the drill master's role instead of watching from behind the line beside Ramayyan. Costume continuity also breaks: the firing soldiers wear red sashes, cross-belts and some red turbans, unlike the plain white men of 4.2, and a plain white flag flies on a fort tower. Passes: Nagoji's ear is a flush stud, chin clean-shaven, boots, talwar, sleeves down; the line is side-on and fires toward off-panel right with muzzle flashes and smoke; no text; open sky for the caption.
decisions.correction: Add the drill master from the previous panel as a third, unnamed figure: a stocky, short, older European, bare-headed, with grizzled dark hair tied back, stubble and a soft belly, in a long-skirted, faded and stained brown coat with deep cuffs over a buff waistcoat and knee breeches. He, not Nagoji, stands at the near (left) end of the firing line, a step back and well clear of the muzzles, one arm flung down and his mouth open on the word of command. Nagoji does NOT give the command. He stands quietly beside Ramayyan at the far left edge of the frame, behind the line, mouth closed, arms at his sides or folded behind his back, simply watching. He wears his rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves down, broad red sash, talwar and boots, and his ear ornament stays a tiny flush gold stud. The firing soldiers wear white tunics, white trousers and white turbans like the men of the previous panel, with no red turbans. No flag on the fort. Keep the side-on line firing as one toward off-panel right, the muzzle flashes, the white sheet of smoke rolling right, the red laterite fort with sloping tiled gatehouse roofs, and the open sky at upper right for the caption.

decisions.issues: Hard checks pass: Nagoji's ear is a tiny flush gold stud; chin clean-shaven with thick curled moustache; sleeves down; talwar; feet out of frame. His eyes cut sidelong toward Ramayyan, as the script asks. Ramayyan matches his sheet, with a composed, unmoved face and palm-leaf bundle and stylus. Smoke is thinning over the line; no text; hands are sound; plenty of sky at the top for both short balloons. Minor: the background soldiers wear dark turbans and are still aiming, unlike the white turbans in 4.2 and 4.5. A plain white marker flag on a pole stands at top left of the drill ground; the letterer can cover it with Nagoji's balloon. Ramayyan is also glancing sideways at Nagoji.

Hard checks pass: Nagoji's ear is a tiny flush gold stud; chin clean-shaven with thick curled moustache; sleeves down; talwar; feet out of frame. Ramayyan turns to Nagoji and speaks, matching his sheet. The line behind them reloads (muskets upright, hands raised to the muzzles), in white with white turbans like 4.2. Same red laterite fort with tiled gatehouse roof; no flag; no text; hands are sound; open sky at top centre for the balloon. Minor: the soldiers wear red waist sashes that the men in 4.2 lacked, and the ramrods are not clearly drawn.

Minor only. The tiny flag on the distant white fort is orange-white-orange, not the plain red, white and blue banded Dutch flag shown in 5.3. Ibrahim's scar does not read because his far (left) cheek is turned away in this wide shot. Everything else passes: Ibrahim matches his sheet (white turban, grey-flecked beard, teal short coat over the pocketed vest, mundu, sandals). He is shouting at a boatman heaving a barrel into a loaded boat, with poled boats on a backwater. No text, sound hands. Clear sky top-centre for the caption and balloon.

Script beat fails twice. (1) Ibrahim greets with joined palms (namaste) instead of touching his forehead in a salaam as scripted. (2) He faces camera-right, so his RIGHT cheek is toward the camera and the scar from his left ear to the jaw never reads, against the script's three-quarter left-cheek framing. Everything else passes. Nagoji: tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, rust-red turban, sleeves down, red sash, boots, talwar. Ramayyan: plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundle, stylus. Quay setting matches 5.1. No text.
decisions.correction: Ibrahim greets with a Muslim salaam, not joined palms: his right hand is raised with the fingertips touching his own forehead, palm inward, and his left hand rests at his side. No namaste, no pressed palms. Stage Nagoji and Ramayyan arriving from the LEFT of the frame and put Ibrahim on the RIGHT, turned three-quarter toward camera-left to face them. That way his anatomical LEFT cheek faces the camera and the thin scar from his left ear down to the jaw reads clearly, never on his right cheek. Keep everything that worked. The setting stays the sunlit backwater quay with the tiled awning, barrels and boats. Nagoji stays in his rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves to the wrists, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots and sheathed talwar, with a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a tiny flush gold ear stud with nothing hanging. Ramayyan stays in plain white cloth with his palm-leaf bundle and stylus. Ibrahim keeps his white turban, grey-flecked beard, teal short coat over the cream pocketed vest, and white mundu. Leave open sky above the heads for two balloons, and no text anywhere.

decisions.issues: v01 fails the ear check: the gold piece sits at the bottom edge of the lobe and reads as a small hanging drop. v02 passes every hard check. The ear is now a small flush gold stud with nothing hanging. Chin is clean-shaven (light stipple only). He wears boots, sleeves are down, no brand shows, and he carries the talwar, rust-red turban and red sash. The setting is the bund between paddy and backwater in late gold light, with no text or anachronism, and the upper-right sky is clear for both Ramayyan lines. Minor issues, not failures: Ramayyan glances sideways toward Nagoji while gesturing, but the script says he talks without looking at him. Ramayyan wears sandals, while his sheet and the 6.5 pick show him barefoot. The region edit left a faint soft smudge on the jaw just below the ear, which is barely visible at print size.

v01 fails the ear check: a gold drop hangs below the lobe. v02 (a regeneration) passes. Nagoji is seen from behind in lost profile, and his ear shows a tiny flush gold stud. He wears boots, sleeves are down, and he carries the talwar, sash and rust-red turban. The wide high view takes in the hill temple, market awnings, a drill ground with small white-clad troops (no redcoats), backwaters and the westering sun. Only the red laterite fort wall cuts in at the top-left edge. There is no text, and a large clear sky across the top holds both captions. Minor issues, not failures: the fort wall comes down the left edge further than "only the edge cutting into the top of the frame". One small whitewashed building with blue shutters near the drill ground looks faintly European.

v01 fails the ear check: two stacked gold beads hang from the lobe. v02 passes the hard checks. The ear is now a single small gold stud on the lobe. Chin is clean-shaven, he wears boots, sleeves are down, and he carries the talwar. The sea line shows beyond the inlet, Ramayyan stands a step higher on the path and has turned back, there is no text, and the upper-left sky is clear for both lines. Minor issues, not failures: a faint pale skin-tone dot from the removed lower bead remains just below the stud (2 to 3 px, it does not read as gold). Nagoji looks over his shoulder toward Ramayyan rather than back down at the country. Ramayyan shows a tiny pale stud in his left earlobe that is not on his sheet. Ramayyan wears sandals, as in 6.1. The laterite fort wall stands close beside the path rather than only high above.

Acceptable; only minor issues. Ramayyan glances up and to the right, while the fort sits above and behind him at upper left. The fort flies a plain saffron streamer, single-tailed rather than swallow-tailed and unlettered, where 6.5 shows red pennants. A whitewashed house with European-looking windows stands on the fort wall. The palace behind the bowman in inset 1 has somewhat European or Indo-Islamic detailing, but it is dark and desaturated. Passing: Ramayyan matches his sheet; the three dark insets run along the bottom inside the panel (a bowman crouched on a roof, a hand tipping a vial into a brass lamp with an open wick, a dagger half drawn in a festival crowd); no victims, blood, text or noose; hands sound; clear sky at upper right for both balloons.

v01 fails the ear check: a large gold drop hangs below the lobe. v01 also shows a lighthouse-like tower in the harbour, which may be an anachronism. v02 (a regeneration) passes. The ear is a small flush gold stud, the chin is clean-shaven, he wears boots, sleeves are down, and he carries the talwar. Ramayyan taps the palm-leaf bundle with one finger. The fort wall rises high above them with plain unlettered red pennants, and dusk comes in over the sea with lateen-sailed boats. Hands are sound and there is no text. The upper-right sky is clear for both Ramayyan lines. Minor issue: Ramayyan is barefoot here, which matches his sheet but not the sandals he wears in 6.1 and 6.3.

All hard checks pass. Nagoji has a flush gold stud on the lobe with nothing hanging, a thick curled moustache, a clean chin, sleeves down to the wrists, the rust-red turban, red sash and talwar. His feet are out of frame, so the boots cannot be seen. Ramayyan matches his sheet (receding hair, white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus). He stands on the threshold and looks back at Nagoji, with the lamplit hall open behind them. The lamps are brass with open wicks. There is no text, no chair and no anachronism. Soft notes: (1) the seated men have brass cups and banana leaves with flowers, not palm-leaf manuscripts; (2) a tiny lamp flame peeks out just behind the crown of Ramayyan's head and reads as background. Lettering space is the roof-beam area at top centre and the dusk sky at top right, above Ramayyan.

All hard checks pass. The ear ornament is a tiny flush stud on the lobe with nothing hanging. He has the thick curled moustache, a clean chin (faint shading only), sleeves to the wrists, boots, rust-red turban, red sash and cream trousers. His left hand rests on the talwar hilt at his hip, and the anatomy is sound. It is the same hall as 7.1 and 7.3: tiger-carved doorjambs, brass lamps with open wicks, men seated with brass vessels. There is no text and no chair. Soft notes: (1) the sky is a warm orange sunset with the sun on the horizon, while 7.1 and 7.3 show a violet dusk, a small lighting shift; (2) the shot is full figure rather than close. Open sky at upper right holds Nagoji's balloon.

Clean on the hard checks. Ramayyan matches his sheet and is alone in the panel. He stands half turned toward the lamplit hall and gives a measuring sideways look. The hall has the same tiger-carved jambs and dusk sea as 7.1. Hanging and standing lamps are brass with open wicks. There is no text, no chair and no anachronism, and the hands with stylus and bundle are sound. Soft notes: (1) one background man, seated with his back to camera, wears a rust-red turban. His bare arm, maroon shoulder cloth and mundu do not match Nagoji's costume, so he should not read as Nagoji, but the author may want to know; (2) Ramayyan's eyes go to frame right, while in 7.1 Nagoji stood to his left, a mild screen-direction shift. Lettering space: the sky and eave at top centre-left for the two balloons, and the plain stone steps at the bottom for the caption.

v02 passes every hard check. All three Nagojis wear a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging (checked at high zoom), have clean-shaven chins, and wear the commander outfit with sleeves down, boots and a talwar. Each band shows a bay with a black mane, tail and lower legs and no white markings. All three beats are there: a river ford in driving rain, a dusty pass under a hard sun, and monsoon mud. There is no text or anachronism, the hands are sound, and the sky at the top centre and the rainy sky at the top left are clear for both captions. Minor: in the mud band only a background rider is clearly hauling at the bridle. v01 fails because every Nagoji ear has a hanging gold drop.

v02 passes every hard check. Nagoji's ear has a flush round gold stud with nothing hanging; it is a little larger than on the sheet but still a stud. His chin is clean-shaven and he wears the commander outfit with sleeves down, boots and a talwar. Padmini wears a cotton sari with a gold border in the old drape with no blouse. Her black hair is coiled at the nape, with simple gold and her walking stick. The heavy-set Nair chieftain stands on his threshold in red-bordered cloth with gold ear rings. An empty bullock cart and a column of lancers with lances upright are present. There are no European chairs, no text and no anachronism, and the hands are sound. The sky at the top centre and the plain dirt road at the bottom left hold the three captions. Minor deviations: Nagoji stands in the road rather than right at a gatepost, the lancers wear white turbans, and their mounts are full-sized horses, some with white blazes, rather than small ponies; Nagoji is not mounted, so the blazes do not matter for Kayal. v01 fails because Nagoji's ear has a hanging gold drop.

v01 fails three checks. (1) Nagoji's ear: a gold ball drop hangs below the lobe, not a flush stud (hard fail). (2) Every horseman behind him wears his rust-red turban, cream tunic and red sash, so the Maravars read as Nagoji clones. That breaks the Maravar look set in 7.5 (white head cloths, brown short jackets, white mundus, lances) and blurs who is Nagoji. (3) The inset shows a broad wood-grain board, not a palm leaf. The rest passes: clean chin, sleeves down, boots, talwar drawn, Kayal a correct bay with black points and no white, wet bamboo at a gallop, no text.
decisions.correction: Nagoji's ear has only a tiny gold stud set flush on the lobe, with nothing hanging below it: no ball, bead, drop or ring. Only Nagoji wears the rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers and boots. The Maravar horsemen behind him must match the lancers on page 7: white or off-white head cloths (never rust-red or red turbans), brown or ochre short jackets over white mundus hitched for riding, no red sashes, no cream trousers, bare lower legs, on small light ponies, carrying lances or short swords. In the inset, show a real dried palm leaf (olai): a long, narrow, pale straw-yellow strip with fine parallel fibres along its length and a small binding hole near one end, not a wooden board.
